transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Patel. What brings you in today?
I feel drained all the time, like I never have the energy to get through work or even enjoy the things I used to. It has just gotten to the point where everything feels like a massive effort.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities, even things you used to enjoy?

Yes, absolutely. I've completely stopped playing soccer, hiking, and cooking for my friends, which are all things I used to love. Now, I just end up turning down their invitations because I don't have the interest or energy to show up anymore.
Have you also been feeling down, sad, or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Yes, I've felt that way almost every day, but it has been going on for much longer than two weeks—more like over two years now. It's like this constant dull heaviness in my chest, like a gray filter over everything where I just feel numb and detached even when good things happen.
How long have you been feeling this way with the low mood and lack of interest—specifically, has it been present most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years?

Yes, it has been pretty much continuous for a little over two years now, starting around the middle of my second year of college. It doesn't really come and go; it is there almost every single day as a constant, dull heaviness and lack of energy.
During this two-year period, have there been any periods lasting six months or more where you felt noticeably better, even if just for a while?
No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. This heavy, drained feeling has been continuous and unbroken for the entire two years, without any periods of relief or feeling better.

The patient reports a persistent low mood and loss of interest lasting over two years without any significant periods of improvement, which aligns with the diagnostic criteria for persistent mood disorder (dysthymia) under F34.1. There is no indication of major depressive episode with full remission or other mood disorders such as bipolar disorder or cyclothymia. The chronicity, continuity, and absence of symptom-free intervals support maintaining F34.1 as the only candidate.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic, low-grade depressed mood with marked anhedonia and fatigue persisting for over two years without any symptom-free intervals, meeting duration and symptom criteria for persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). Major depressive episode and recurrent depressive disorder were considered but ruled out due to the chronic, continuous nature without episodic remission.
